strategy.summary: Reproduce astropy PR 17693 by building astropy from source at buggy commit 841824ce8f0f (not the PyPI wheel) and applying only the developer's test. On the buggy revision, theta for rho=1 m, z=1e8 m comes out as exactly 0 because z/r rounds to 1.0 in float64 and arccos(1.0)=0, so assert_allclose against 1e-8 rad fails. On the fixed revision arctan2(rho,z) gives about 1e-8 rad and the test passes. The defect is a total loss of the value (0 versus 1e-8), not a last-bit difference, so the result does not depend on tolerance choice.

system_packages: gcc or clang with C/C++ toolchain
build_commands: git clone https://github.com/astropy/astropy.git && cd astropy && git checkout 841824ce8f0f
git apply the test diff from PR 17693 onto the buggy checkout (only tests/test_representation.py)
pip install -e . --no-build-isolation (or pip install -e . after build deps are present)
pinned_because: numpy: no documented constraint; version chosen as numpy 2.x because the PR is from the numpy-2 era of astropy development, inferred not documented; the defect depends only on float64 arithmetic and arccos/arctan2, which are stable across numpy versions
astropy: no pin; it is built from source at the buggy commit because the released wheel may already contain the fix or differ from the buggy revision
python 3.12: chosen as a current interpreter supported by the dev branch; not stated in evidence

strategy.reproducing_test: test_to_physicsspherical_small_theta in astropy/coordinates/tests/test_representation.py (added after test_to_physicsspherical_at_the_origin): cyl = CylindricalRepresentation(rho=1*u.m, phi=10*u.deg, z=1e8*u.m); got = cyl.represent_as(PhysicsSphericalRepresentation); assert_allclose on got.r vs 1e8 m, got.phi vs 10 deg, got.theta vs 1e-8 rad
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy commit 841824ce8f0f the test FAILS: got.theta is 0 rad (arccos(z/r) with z/r == 1.0 exactly), and assert_allclose against 1e-8 rad fails because the absolute error 1e-8 exceeds the relative tolerance 1e-7*1e-8 with atol 0. On the fixed revision (theta = arctan2(rho, z)) the test PASSES: theta is about 1e-8 rad to float64 precision, and r and phi assertions also pass.
strategy.numerical_probe: Before running pytest on the buggy checkout, run in Python: from astropy.coordinates import CylindricalRepresentation, PhysicsSphericalRepresentation; import astropy.units as u; CylindricalRepresentation(1*u.m, 0*u.deg, 1e8*u.m).represent_as(PhysicsSphericalRepresentation).theta, expecting 0 rad on buggy and about 1e-8 rad on fixed.
risks: Installing astropy from PyPI instead of building commit 841824ce8f0f from source will not reproduce the bug or the test; the test file must come from the buggy checkout with the test diff applied.
Build failures from missing compiler or Cython/extension-helpers versions will prevent import; the test cannot run until the C extensions are built.

numpy version is not documented; numpy 2.x was chosen by era inference, not stated evidence. The arccos(1.0)=0 behaviour is IEEE-standard so the transition should hold on any numpy version, but this is inferred.

Platform dependence is not expected: float64 hypot and z/r both round to exactly 1e8 and 1.0, so the defect should appear on x86_64 and arm64 alike. No sanitizer or 32-bit build is needed. If the representation code computes r through a different path that yields a value other than 1e8 exactly, z/r could differ from 1.0, so run the numerical probe first to confirm the buggy value is 0.

No tolerance or dtype is stated in the evidence. assert_allclose default rtol=1e-7 is assumed; the transition is robust because the buggy value is 0 and the expected value is 1e-8, a complete loss rather than a rounding difference.
The regression test also checks r and phi; if those assertions fail on the buggy revision for a reason unrelated to theta, the transition is muddied, so verify they pass on both revisions.
Test selection with -k must match the new test name exactly; if the class fixture or parametrization differs in the checkout, the test may be collected as zero items.

oracle.tolerance: assert_allclose default rtol=1e-7 assumed (tolerance not stated in evidence)
oracle.reference_source: analytic value atan(rho/z) = 1e-8 rad, as given by the developer's test
oracle.why: Expected theta is the small angle 1e-8 rad; the buggy value 0 differs by 100% so any reasonable relative tolerance separates them.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: got.theta is 0 rad because arccos(z/r) gives arccos(1.0)=0 when z/r rounds to exactly 1.0; assert_allclose(0 rad, 1e-8 rad) fails since the error is far beyond rtol*1e-8 with no atol.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: theta = arctan2(1 m, 1e8 m) is about 1e-8 rad to float64 precision, within rtol 1e-7; r is about 1e8 m and phi is 10 deg, both matching.
